title: Correlation between the Micro/Mycobiome of the Upper Gastrointestinal Tract and the Occurrence of Anastomotic Leaks Following Abdominothoracic Esophageal Resection - A Prospective, Singel-Center Observational Study
summary: Numerous bacteria and fungi live in the mouth, the gastrointestinal tract, and on many other surfaces of the body. Among other things, these microorganisms can influence inflammatory responses, the body’s immune function, and possibly also tissue healing. We aim to investigate whether the composition of these bacteria and fungi in patients with esophageal cancer influences treatment and healing following surgery. To this end, swabs from the mouth and rectum, as well as blood samples, will be analyzed before and after preoperative treatment with medication or radiation therapy. During surgery, a swab will also be taken from the surgical specimen that has already been removed. The results will then be compared with the response to therapy and the subsequent course of the disease after surgery. Our long-term goal is to identify patients at increased risk for complications earlier and, in the future, potentially provide more targeted preventive treatment.
conditions: Planned abdominothoracic esophageal resection for esophageal cancer

interventions.name: In patients with esophageal cancer being treated with curative intent, as part of which neoadjuvant therapy (chemotherapy or radiation) is administered, samples are collected at three time points. These time points are before the start of neoadjuvant therapy, before surgery, and intraoperatively. Or

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned abdominothoracic esophageal resection
Legal capacity
Written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years
Pregnancy
Lack of consent
Emergency surgery
